# Screenwalk

Screenwalk maps a running web application's actual UI, routes, observed transitions, capture gaps, and browser diagnostics into a local visual workspace.

## Start here

- Product and quickstart: README.md
- Documentation home: apps/docs/index.md
- Five-minute first run: apps/docs/guide/quickstart.md
- Framework cookbook: apps/docs/guide/frameworks.md

- Current system research: docs/research/2026-08-14-remotion-devx-performance-and-launch.md

## Safe run

1. Keep the target app running on localhost.
2. Run `pnpm screenwalk doctor /absolute/path/to/app --url http://127.0.0.1:3000 --json`, then `pnpm screenwalk /absolute/path/to/app --url http://127.0.0.1:3000 --no-open --watch`.
   For a password or test-login gate, add `--setup /absolute/path/to/setup.json`; recipes reference secret environment variable names with `valueFromEnv` and never contain the values themselves.
3. Open the printed Studio URL.
4. Use All screens for topology, From Home for entry-reachable branches, Screen library for the capture gallery, and Review findings for evidence and diagnostics.
5. Use Select screens to build a bounded handoff, then copy routes/files or a ready-to-paste agent prompt. Treat unconnected routes as review candidates, not automatic deletion candidates.
6. For capture profiling, pass `--timing-json /tmp/screenwalk-timings.json`; never accept a faster run if it drops useful screens, observed transitions, or populated UI.

## Evidence language

- static: found in source; not proof that a user can reach it at runtime.
- observed: a browser interaction or rendered link was recorded.
- captured: a desktop or mobile screenshot exists for that run.
- access view: an independently captured public or allowed browser context; evidence never crosses between them.
- unobserved or code-only: a known state without current browser proof.

Screenwalk captures versioned snapshots from localhost. Watch mode recaptures changed known routes and keeps the last good graph visible on failure; it is not proof that every transient state has been observed.

## Documentation rule

Use the task-shaped guide before reading internals. The README explains why and proves the outcome; `apps/docs/guide/` teaches workflows; `apps/docs/reference/` defines mechanical contracts. Do not infer a capability from roadmap or research notes when the supported-app matrix says it is deferred.

The docs build also emits `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt`, and raw `/markdown/**` pages for external agents. They are generated from the same user-facing Markdown and must pass `pnpm docs:check`.
